data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Synthetic anabolic steroids with fibrinolytic activity

## Mechanism of action
- Increase hepatic synthesis of C1-esterase inhibitor (hereditary angioedema prophylaxis)
- Enhance fibrinolysis (stanozolol) — used in lipodermatosclerosis and cryofibrinogenaemia

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Hereditary angioedema long-term prophylaxis (older choice; now C1-INH, lanadelumab, berotralstat preferred)
- Lipodermatosclerosis, livedoid vasculopathy, cryofibrinogenaemia (stanozolol — off-label; withdrawn in many countries)
- Raynaud, chronic urticaria (danazol — limited)

## Dose & formulations
- Stanozolol 2–5 mg twice daily (historic); danazol 200 mg/day (HAE, reduce to lowest effective)

## Adverse effects
- Virilisation in women (hirsutism, acne, voice change), menstrual irregularity
- Hepatotoxicity, peliosis hepatis, hepatic adenoma; dyslipidaemia; fluid retention, hypertension

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy, children, liver disease, prostate/breast cancer

## Drug interactions
- Warfarin (INR rises), cyclosporine levels rise

## Monitoring
- LFT, lipids, liver ultrasound (long-term)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated.

## Viva points
- Androgens raise C1-INH levels in hereditary angioedema
- Stanozolol in lipodermatosclerosis (fibrinolytic)

_Sources: Khopkar (Stanozolol); Wolverton 4e ch.40. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
